display.title: Episode 270: The Storyteller, Final Chapter (Shabbos Mevarchim Nissan)
display.summary_short: A boy's essay on hearing the Aseres HaDibros in shul wins a miniature Sefer Torah, a seven-year-old leads the Shema, and The Storyteller reaches its surprising end.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Nissan 5747. Uncle Yossi opens the mailbox full of essays about hearing the Aseres HaDibros read in shul on Parshas Yisro. The winning essay, by a boy whose father has read the Torah in shul for many years, says he closed his eyes and felt he was standing at Har Sinai, and adds that his little sister marches with a spoon and a pot during the Hakochainik march. He wins a miniature Sefer Torah. After the march and a sponsor message, story time brings the climax of The Storyteller. Rabbi Yehudah finishes his one remembered story: the Baal Shem Tov revealed to the feared official Alex that he was really a Jew named Yitzchak, and promised that on the day someone would come and tell him this very story, he would know Hashem had fully forgiven him. In the middle, a seven-year-old yeshiva boy who loves saying the Twelve Pesukim leads the Shema. Then the wealthy Reb Yitzchak stands up in tears: he is that man, and this is the day. He shares his wealth with Rabbi Yehudah, fulfilling the Baal Shem Tov's blessing, and Rabbi Yehudah and his wife rejoice that they can now give tzedakah generously. The show ends with a new Shabbos Candle Lighting Club and a reminder to hear Parshas HaChodesh.
display.lesson: Hashem's ways are wondrous: patience and trust in a tzaddik's blessing are rewarded, and it is never too late to return to Hashem.
